Mr. Amit Kundra, Advocate for respondent No.3-Insurance Company.

ok 36 ok Ritu Tagore, J
1.

The legal heirs (claimants-appellants) of deceased Vijay Singh are in appeal against the award dated 01.03.2016 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Rewari (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal'), on the ground of inadequate compensation.

2. Deceased Vijay Singh, a sole breadwinner of the family of claimants, died in a motor vehicular accident dated 25.06.2013 caused by respondent No.1/driver while driving the offending vehicle TATA Safari bearing registration No.HR-36P-5708, in a rash and negligent manner.
3.
The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
The respondents (driver, owner and insurer) put up an appearance and filed their respective pleadings.

On the basis of the evidence, the Tribunal recorded a positive finding in favor of claimants and against the respondent No.1-driver on issue of rash and negligent driving of the offending MANPREET SINGH 2023.03.2209:24 Vehicle and awarded a sum of Rs.7,19,500/- as compensation along with | attest to the accuracy and authenticity of this order/judgment FAO-5053 of 2016 2023:PHHC:040903 2 interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realisation and made the respondents jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award.
4. Aggrieved with the award of the Tribunal, claimants have preferred this appeal for enhancement of compensation.

5. The principal grounds on which the present appeal has been preferred are:

sentences.text: i) The Tribunal has erred in holding the income of deceased at Rs.5,500/- p.m. and did not take the actual income of Rs.65,000/-p.m. of the deceased from agriculture and prayed that award amount is liable to be enhanced after taking the actual income of the deceased.
ii) Future prospects were not taken into consideration by the Tribunal as per 'National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others' (2017) 16 SCC 680.

iv) Compensation on the conventional heads, i.e. loss of consortium to widow and children, loss of estate, funeral expenses etc. has not been granted as per the observations made in 'Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu_Ram @ Chuhru_Ram and others' (2018) 18 SCC 130.

6. A prayer was accordingly made to enhance the amount of compensation.

7. however, failed to dispute the contention as raised above that grant of compensation on the conventional heads is not as per the legal proposition expounded by the Hon'ble Apex Court.
8.
I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the record and paper book.

9. Claimants have pleaded that deceased was cultivating about 28 acres of land; out of which 4 acres of land was owned by deceased, 9 acres of land belonging to his brothers and 15 acres land of others.

Besides the above, deceased was also running a milk dairy and was earning about Rs.65,000/- p.m.
cumulatively from all the above sources.

10. Rameshwar Dayal, brother of deceased (PW-2) and Rajesh Devi widow of deceased (PW-3)
admitted that they have no documentary proof to show that deceased was doing the claimed work and had income of Rs.65,000/- p.m. as alleged.
The copy of revenue record of the year 2012-13 (Exh.PW-3/B) does not record the deceased as owner of the land.
Petitioner No.1 his wife has been recorded as a co-sharer in the record of rights.
No perceptible evidence has been led on record to show that deceased had the claimed earnings.
The Tribunal has thus, rightly taken his income on notional basis at Rs.5,500/- p.m. by treating him as an unskilled worker.

Sr. Heads Amount in Rs.

2. 10% future prospects Rs.550/-
3. 1/4" deduction towards personal Rs.4,538/- expenses (Rs.6,050-Rs.1,512)
4.
Total income Rs.4,538- 5. Multiplier 11 i.e. Rs.4,538 x 12 x 11 Rs.5,99,016/- (being the age 51 years)

6. Loss of estate and funeral expenses Rs.33,000/- (Rs.16,500/- each )
7.

| Loss of consortium (spousal, filial and Rs.1,76,000/- parental) i.e. (Rs.44,000/- x 4)
8.

9.

| Enhanced amount of compensation Rs.88,516 /-
12.
The liability of the Insurance Company is also not in dispute in this appeal.

The respondent No.3-Insurance company, is hereby directed to pay the claimants-appellants an enhanced amount of compensation i.e. Rs.88,516/- (Rupees eighty eight thousand five hundred and sixteen only)
awarded hereinabove, over and above, the amount awarded by the Tribunal, at the rate of interest as granted by the Tribunal from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realisation, and deposit the awarded amount within a period of two months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment, with the Tribunal.
The remaining conditions of disbursal of the amount as given by the Tribunal shall remain unaltered.
Needless to mention that the amount, if any, already deposited by the insurance company shall be MANPREET SINGH adjusted.
